sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry, Mark Van de Velde, Tope Olagunju & Bitrus Andrew. 2017. Results of the first AdaGram survey in Adamawa and Taraba States, Nigeria. Slides, 47th Colloquium on African Languages and Linguistics, Leiden. 33 slides.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. Two slides 'SABON GIDA DUNA: FAM' give the name as [fám]; before the survey only 'wordlist ca. 70 words' (Blench 2011 ms) existed; after it 'wordlist ca. 700 words with audio', 'ca. 140 phrases with audio', and 'Tope has written his BA term paper on the basic description of Fam'.
sources.venue: Slides, 47th Colloquium on African Languages and Linguistics, Leiden. 33 slides

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014 [2011]. Fam wordlist with Ndoola corresponding terms (and etymological commentary). 4 pp. ms. Cambridge: KWEF.
sources.note: The only published primary data; would show whether tone or accent is marked and any transcription note. Reported untoned (Wikipedia; AdaGram slides), so low chance of a stress statement.
sources.venue: Fam wordlist with Ndoola corresponding terms (and etymological commentary). 4 pp. ms

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014 [file dated 24 April 2011]. Fam wordlist with Ndoola corresponding terms [running head: 'Fam wordlist and etymological commentary', circulation draft]. 4 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: No stress or tone statement. The introduction says verbatim: 'This data was when my linguistic skills were rudimentary, hence the lack of tone-marking.' - i.e. the ca. 75-item list (recorded 1984) is untoned by the author's admission (tone presupposed, not described). Phonology content is limited to: 'The presence of the dental fricative /θ/ is characteristic of Jukunoid and atypical for Mambiloid languages' and 'some evidence of Jukun contact in the phonology'; morphology: plural -bə, a- prefixes, 'complete loss of noun-class apparatus'. A handful of Fam forms carry stray diacritics (àʧóò 'f…

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. n.d. [c. 2011]. The North Bantoid hypothesis. Draft circulated for comment. Cambridge: KWEF. Sec. 2.2.1 and Fig. 3.
sources.note: Nothing on Fam phonology: 'Connell (p.c.) remains doubtful about the inclusion of the poorly documented Fam language'; 'the membership of Fam in Mambiloid is highly uncertain'. The Mambiloid phonology subsection (2.2.2) does not discuss Fam.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011. The membership and internal structure of Bantoid and the border with Bantu. PowerPoint presentation (40 slides), Bantu IV (B4ntu), Humboldt University, Berlin, 7-9 April 2011. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Nothing on Fam prosody. Fam appears only as a classificatory label: 'Ndoro-Fam?' as a node of the Bantoid tree, 'Fam' on the map of Mambiloid languages (Nigeria side, next to Ndoro), and as a leaf (Ndoro, Fam, Nizaa, Kwanja.. under Proto-Mambiloid) in the genetic tree of Mambiloid. The only occurrence of 'tone' in the deck is the general remark that some north-western languages 'must simply be excised from Bantu if the standard views of phonology, tone, etc. are to be maintained' (slide 'Is the concept of Bantu on life-support II?'), unrelated to Fam. No stress/accent statement anywhere.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2009. The Bantoid Languages [draft monograph, 'DRAFT ONLY - NOT TO BE QUOTED WITHOUT PERMISSION'; file 'Bantoid languages ', created 2009-07-20]. 51 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. (Glottolog ref 24122.)
sources.note: Nothing on Fam phonology, tone or stress. The only tone passages concern Ambele (Grassfields) and bibliography entries. Fam appears at p. 13 (quoted), in Figure 6 and on the Mambiloid map only.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 1997. The Integrity of Mambiloid. Paper presented at the Second World Congress of African Linguistics, Leipzig, 27 July - 3 August 1997 (Institute of Social and Cultural Anthropology, Oxford). HTML version hosted on Mambila Studies (mambila.info, ed. D. Zeitlyn).
sources.note: Nothing for Fam. The only prosodic content is family-level ('Mambiloid languages appear all to have either three or four tones. The four tone systems are plausibly a development of an earlier three tone system..'; suffix tone copying the stem in Mambila lects; Connell 1997a tonal split) and Fam is explicitly excluded from the languages considered; no stress/accent mention anywhere (0 matches).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 1993. An outline classification of the Mambiloid languages. Journal of West African Languages 23(1): 105-118. Sec. 1.7 'Fam' p. 109; sec. 2.2 'Tone' pp. 110-111; sec. 4 p. 116.
sources.note: Nothing on Fam stress. Sec. 1.7: 'Only a short wordlist was collected and it has not been possible to return'. Sec. 2.2 is a family-level tone note ('the group is exceptional for the complexity of its tonal systems and the prevalence of phonemic contour tones') citing Vute, Kwanja and Mambila only; Fam is not mentioned there. Sec. 4 gives two Ndoro-Fam lexical comparisons, untoned.
